cells.tense: Right now the connection is real and it is being chosen, with the ink wet.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When someone questions the direction you've already chosen here, say what you're keeping rather than re-deciding it. One sentence is enough. Say it plainly; you don't have to win the room.
cells.core:
Two streams have met here and you've seen enough to move with it, so the direction isn't in question — the week leaning on it is. Where you can't see the whole road, you don't need to. You need the next step, and you've been taking it, and what you chose in the fog is holding.

The work now is keeping the heading when it's contested. Not arguing anyone down — just not re-opening the question whenever someone leans on it. Say what you're keeping, once, then let that stand. The pull off course comes in small pieces and looks reasonable. What you have is momentum you gathered by feeling your way, and it's yours to hold without dressing it up.
cells.sheetLine: What you chose in the fog, you get to keep choosing.
cells.verb: choosing two streams and letting them run as one
cells.place: in the fog where the next step is the only thing lit

cells.tense: Ahead of you the connection hasn't arrived yet, and you're already braced for what it will demand.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: With something you've already grown here — a friendship, a project, a habit — stop tending it for one evening and just use it. Sit with what's there. Don't improve it; don't plan its next stage.
cells.core:
The meeting is imagined before it happens and managed before it's felt. You're rehearsing what you'll say and how you'll be received, and the rehearsals have gotten further out than the actual contact can carry. Vision is running without the experience it's supposed to come from.

What you have here was grown carefully — slowly, on purpose, over a long stretch — and it's finished enough to stand on. The next move is to enjoy it. Not to plan the next stage, not to improve it. Use what you made, let it be seen, let someone else get the benefit of it. Care that keeps clutching isn't care anymore. The abundance is real; resting in it is how the connection gets room to actually arrive.
cells.sheetLine: What you've grown is ready. Let it be used.
cells.verb: choosing two streams and letting them run as one
cells.place: in the fog where the next step is the only thing lit

cells.tense: You were standing at a meeting that has already happened, still waiting to be let through.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Take a belief you hold about this connection — a hope, a rule, a fear — and trace where you first heard it. If it doesn't lead back to your own life, set it down this week and notice what shifts.
cells.core:
The connection is real, and you pulled back from it before the meeting could finish. The pairing got left where it was. Where you navigate by not-quite-seeing, the fog has become a place you live rather than a stretch you're crossing. There's a next step here, and it's been sitting there.

The starved thing isn't effort; it's knowing what you actually think. So don't push feeling back into it. Instead, look at the assumptions you carry about this connection — the hopes, the rules, the worries — and sort which are yours and which you picked up somewhere else. Some will be secondhand. Set those down, and the direction you're actually standing in becomes visible without your having to force it.
cells.sheetLine: The meeting is behind you. What's yours is still here.
cells.verb: choosing two streams and letting them run as one
cells.place: in the fog where the next step is the only thing lit

cells.tense: You're steering this connection already, and you'd tell it that you're not.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Think of someone near you lost on a decision about their own connection. Walk it with them — tell them the route, then go the first stretch alongside. When they've got it, step back and watch them carry on.
cells.core:
The choice here is being made, and you don't register making it. You say you're following where it goes, and the direction is one you're holding — the small adjustments, the weight shifted, the thing you didn't say. From the inside it feels like watching. From the outside it's a hand on the wheel.

What a direction needs isn't more steering from you. It needs to be named, once, to someone. Tell one person the path you'd walk through this, plainly, then leave them to walk it. Don't check their pace, don't adjust the route mid-sentence for how they're taking it. Guidance done well points and steps back. You'll learn your own heading by hearing it in your voice, said to someone else, with no grip on the outcome.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering while saying you're only following.
cells.verb: choosing two streams and letting them run as one
cells.place: in the fog where the next step is the only thing lit
